newsitem.title: USA: Farley's "Ninja" packs punch at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: Farley's "Ninja" packs punch at U.S. box office.

text.p: A bumbling martial arts expert overpowered a wise-cracking San Francisco cop at the weekend box office as "Beverly Hills Ninja" opened in the top spot, according to studio estimates released Sunday.

"Beverly Hills Ninja," a comedy starring Chris Farley, earned an estimated $10 million during the Friday to Sunday period, while Eddie Murphy's "Metro" opened in second with about $9.3 million. Final data will be released on Monday.
The big-screen version of "Evita," starring Madonna and Jonathan Pryce, slipped a notch to third with $7.2 million.

Last week's number one, "The Relic," slid to fifth with $6.7 million, narrowly behind "Jerry Maguire" with $6.8 million. "Maguire," a romantic comedy starring Tom Cruise as a sports agent, passed the $100 million mark on Saturday and now stands at an estimated $102.1 million.

"Beverly Hills Ninja" features Farley as an out-of-shape martial arts hero raised by Ninjas in Japan. It was released by Sony Corp.'s TriStar Pictures unit, and averaged a creditable $4,970 from 2,112 screens.
Several studios said TriStar's estimate was possibly a little optimistic, and the figure was likely closer to the $9.3 million estimated for "Metro."

In "Metro," Murphy plays a San Francisco hostage negotiator in a role that recalls his three "Beverly Hills Cop" movies. Released by Walt Disney Co.'s Touchstone Pictures banner, it averaged $4,648 from 2001 screens.

The movie underwhelmed most critics, although it won raves from the influential Chicago duo of Gene Siskel and Roger Ebert. According to a Variety survey of critics from New York, Los Angeles and Chicago, four critics liked it, 16 did not and three were mixed. Reviews for "Beverly Hills Ninja" were embargoed until Monday, although Variety described it as "surprisingly appealing."

"Evita" earned $7.2 million at the weekend after expanding its screen count to 923 from 704. Its $7,801 screen average was the highest in the top 10. Since opening on Christmas Day in the United States on two screens, it has earned $21.4 million.

According to an executive at Disney, which handles the film in the United States, "Evita" will not expand much further, staying in moderate release and laying the foundation for long-term success. Its fortunes could be bolstered by the Golden Globe awards on Sunday night, when it will compete in five categories. Oscar nominations will be unveiled Feb. 11.

The other new release at the weekend was "Albino Alligator," the directorial debut of Academy Award-winning actor Kevin Spacey. The ensemble crime drama, which stars Faye Dunaway and Matt Dillon, earned an estimated $81,000 from 12 screens, giving it a healthy average of $6,750. The Variety poll showed seven critics liked it, nine did not and 10 were mixed. Disney-owned Miramax Films is releasing the movie.
Sony distributes "Jerry Maguire," while "The Relic" is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc.. The latter has a 10-day tally of $18.7 million.
